acceptance_criteria.text: Given a DPDP erasure request for subject_id S, When DELETE /tenants/{tenant_id}/subjects/{subject_id} is called, Then every item_id associated with S across Zones 1/2/3/6/7/8 is resolved via the new SubjectToItemIndex implementation and enters UnifiedSubjectErasureOrchestrator's cascade -- not only Zone 8 as the live endpoint does today.

Given Zone 8's per-subject encryption key, When the cascade reaches Zone 8, Then zone8_crypto_shredding.py's existing key-destroy primitive continues to be called for real via SubjectErasureCascadeService, exactly as it already is today -- this story does not touch or regress the existing Zone 8 leg. CORRECTED 2026-09-22, solution-architect review round 6: the original claim that this would be 'the first call site anywhere in the codebase' invoking the primitive was false -- SubjectErasureCascadeService already does this, live, today.

Given the erasure job may be long-running, When DELETE is called, Then the response is 202 JobAccepted per openapi.yaml's existing contract, pollable via the existing GET /jobs/{job_id}, exactly as it already is today for the Zone-8-only path -- this story extends the SAME job-tracking mechanism to the orchestrator's combined outcome, not a new one.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given the API host is under concurrent load, When multiple requests touch different zones' SQL repositories simultaneously, Then each acquires its own pooled connection rather than contending on one shared object.
Given the pool is exhausted, When a new request needs a connection, Then the API returns 503 + Retry-After, not an indefinite block or crash.
